404 on access denial (not 403) so the framework doesn't leak existence of resources the caller can't see: a table the caller may not read answers exactly what a path with no route answers (`no API route matches this path, or the app's access rules do not let you use it`). A create, update or delete refused on a table the caller MAY read answers 403 `{"error":"forbidden","message":...}` instead (GET already shows the table exists), plus a `hint` when a tenant-less caller writes to a tenant-keyed table. An op set to `off` keeps its 404.
`self` mode lookups by id resolve to 200 for the caller's OWN row regardless of mode floor - /api/_auth/users/{me} always works (a scoped token needs `_benmore_users:read`).

The user directory (GET /api/_auth/users, /api/_auth/users/{id}) is governed by `_benmore_users: read:` (or `default:`), private (`admin`) when nothing is declared: `everyone` lists all active users, `self` only the caller, `admin` everyone for admins and only the caller otherwise, `group` the active members of the caller's tenant, `off` 404. `role:a,b` works there - an admin or a caller holding a listed role GLOBALLY (the users.role column or an un-scoped grant) sees every active user, anyone else only themselves; a role held only inside one tenant does not qualify, because the users table has no tenant column. `group` matches members through groups.user_field whatever it is called (an email column such as `member_email`, or a user-id column). Rows carry every non-secret users column; `password_change_required` (an account still on a temporary password) is returned only to an admin and for the caller's own row. A scoped API token or session (explicit scopes other than '*') needs `_benmore_users:read` (or `*:read`) in its own scopes for both endpoints, its own row included, and gets 403 otherwise; unscoped credentials need nothing extra.
When `read: anon` or `read: everyone` is set on a table with user_id, the implicit owner-WHERE is auto-dropped. No need for scopes.public_read_when.
Per-row mutation gating (owner-WHERE on UPDATE/DELETE) still applies for `self`/`group` modes. The access: block is the COARSE entrance gate; row-level filtering happens after.

Record-level ACL grants (api({at:'permissions'})) OR into the owner-scoped modes but are bounded by the tenant clause on group-keyed tables: a row shared to a user in another tenant stays 404 for them.

Modes are case-insensitive. Unknown modes fail closed: every request for that operation is denied, admins included (403, or 404 when the caller cannot read the table), and the write gate / `benmore check` report the mode as an error; the denial itself is not logged.
